methods.name: PairWithQr
methods.comment:
A connect that fails fails this call itself, with the Status ConnectAccount
gives, before any stream exists (#250).
An account with a stored identity (paired or logged out) gets
FailedPrecondition: it would log in, and no QR or code would ever come
(#253). To pair again, DeleteAccount and CreateAccount; pass the same
external_ref to keep addressing it by that ref. Only the uuid changes.

methods.name: PairWithCode
methods.comment:
A connect that fails fails this call itself, with the Status ConnectAccount
gives, before any stream exists (#250).
An account with a stored identity (paired or logged out) gets
FailedPrecondition: it would log in, and no QR or code would ever come
(#253). To pair again, DeleteAccount and CreateAccount; pass the same
external_ref to keep addressing it by that ref. Only the uuid changes.

methods.name: Logout
methods.comment:
Unlinks the device but keeps the account row and its stored identity,
so the account cannot pair again (see PairWithQr). The core keeps no
reset of its own: delete and create compose it, and external_ref
carries the caller's key across (#255).

services.name: AdminService
services.comment: Admin/observability surface. Exposed via RPC over the socket (no TCP listener).

methods.name: Check
methods.comment: Liveness + readiness for the daemon itself (not per-account WhatsApp state).

services.name: CallService
services.comment:
Call control that needs no media stack. Placing and answering a call do, and
stay out of the core.

methods.name: RejectCall
methods.comment:
Sends one `<call><reject/></call>` stanza. The server answers nothing, so
success means the stanza went out, not that the caller saw the decline:
the `CallEvent` stream shows how the call ended. Whether and when to
reject is the edge's policy.

methods.name: GetPushName
methods.comment:
The account's OWN push name (the getter that pairs with SetPushName).
Takes an AccountRef, not a jid: WhatsApp gives a companion device no
per-contact push-name store, so a jid argument would read as "what is this
contact called" while meaning nothing (issue #1).

methods.name: SetAbout
methods.comment: The account's OWN about text, the setter next to GetAbout (#197).

methods.name: BlockContact
methods.comment:
Block or unblock a user. The jid must be a phone jid
("<user>@s.whatsapp.net") or a LID ("<user>@lid"), relayed as given: any
other kind is InvalidArgument. A block sends both sides of the pair, so it
needs the LID<->PN mapping the client already learned; without it the
answer is FailedPrecondition and nothing is sent. An unblock by LID needs
no mapping (#197).

methods.name: GetBlocklist
methods.comment: The account's blocklist, entry by entry as the server returns it (#197).

methods.name: UnsubscribePresence
methods.comment:
Release a SubscribePresence (#271). The library forgets the jid only after
the unsubscribe stanza is sent, so an error leaves the subscription in
place (it is renewed on the next reconnect): retry to release it.

methods.name: ResolveLidPn
methods.comment:
Targeted LID<->PN lookup, batched. Reads the live client (in-memory cache
first, durable store on miss), so it also sees mappings learned during an
offline history replay, which are cached before they are persisted.

methods.name: ListLidMappings
methods.comment:
Every LID<->PN pair persisted for the account, for a consumer reconciling
its own store in one pass. Reads storage directly, so it answers for a
disconnected account too -- and, being the durable side, it misses the
in-memory-only mappings ResolveLidPn can still answer.

methods.name: SetGroupMembershipApproval
methods.comment: `enabled` true: a new member waits for an admin's approval.

methods.name: MarkRead
methods.comment:
Send a read receipt for `message_ids` from `sender`: the thing that turns
the other person's ticks blue (#20).

One WhatsApp operation per RPC. The official app does this AND syncs its
own devices, but composing the two is the edge's call: bundling them here
would leave no way to ask for one without the other.

Two things the core cannot tell you, both upstream's to expose. WhatsApp
downgrades the receipt to `read-self` when the account has read receipts
switched off in its privacy settings, and only for a private DM -- a group
read goes out as `read` regardless. The library reads that flag off a
device snapshot it does not expose (`persistence_manager` is `pub(crate)`
and there is no getter), so the core cannot report which of the two it
sent. Silence here is not evidence of either.

methods.name: MarkChatRead
methods.comment:
Mark the chat read on THIS account's own linked devices. No receipt, and
nobody else sees it. Not MarkRead, which sends the receipt (#20): a
different operation gets a name of its own.

methods.name: MarkUnread
methods.comment:
Mark a chat unread. Separate from MarkChatRead (which keeps its proto3
default read=true): flipping that bool would be a silent breaking change.

methods.name: StarMessage
methods.comment: Chat actions (synced across the account's linked devices).

methods.name: DeleteChat
methods.comment:
Deletes the whole chat locally (distinct from DeleteMessage, which revokes
a single message for everyone).

methods.name: SendContact
methods.comment: Rich content sends.

methods.name: SendInteractiveReply
methods.comment: Answer a button / list / template / native-flow offer by id (issue #28).

methods.name: SendPollVote
methods.comment:
Vote in a poll (this account's own vote), and tally votes the edge holds.
AggregatePollVotes reads nothing but its request plus the account's
identity store, and sends no stanza -- but it still needs the account
CONNECTED, because that store is reached through the live client.

methods.name: PostStatusText
methods.comment: Status / stories.

methods.name: RevokeStatus
methods.comment:
The answer's key is the revoke stanza's own, like EditMessage's; the
status it revoked is the echo's `protocol_target`.

methods.name: GetStatusAudience
methods.comment:
The status audience the library holds for this account; reads nothing
from the server (#89).

methods.name: ListSubscribedNewsletters
methods.comment:
Every channel this account follows. The startup call: it lets a consumer
name every newsletter row it already holds in one round trip, the way
GroupService.ListParticipating does for groups.

methods.name: GetNewsletterMetadata
methods.comment:
One channel, for a jid that turned up in a message before the list was
fetched. NotFound when no channel exists behind the jid (#56).
PermissionDenied with wa-code 405 when the server refuses the read to
this account, as it did in production for a channel it does not follow.

methods.name: GetNewsletterMessages
methods.comment:
A page of a channel's history (issue #26). Plain IQ, no decryption: a
channel is not E2E, so the server hands back the payloads itself.

It is also the only road to a channel's server-side tallies, and they are
the reason it exists. Those add-ons never arrive as messages — a channel
reaction is a server node, not a `ReactionMessage`, and in 2244 channel
payloads measured on one live store not one carried a
`pollResultSnapshotMessage`. Reaction counts, poll votes and forward counts
are counted by the server and handed over here, and pushed as
NewsletterLiveUpdate events to a subscriber of the channel.

methods.name: SendNewsletterPollVote
methods.comment: Vote in a channel poll, or change or remove the vote (issue #26).

methods.name: GetMyNewsletterAddOns
methods.comment:
This account's own reaction and poll vote per message: the only way to read
back a vote, since the tallies count every follower.

methods.name: SubscribeNewsletterLiveUpdates
methods.comment:
Ask the server to push this channel's tallies as NewsletterLiveUpdate
events, for the answered duration. Without it none arrive. Renewing before
the duration runs out is the caller's timer: the core keeps none.

methods.name: FollowNewsletter
methods.comment:
Follow a channel (#199). Answers nothing: measured live, the server's
answer to the join carries the channel id and not its name, badge or this
account's role, so a Newsletter built from it would state UNVERIFIED for a
verified channel. GetNewsletterMetadata reads the channel as it is.

fields.name: about
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the new text (the library's `status`)

fields.name: jid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The account's own jid (issue #274): the paired device's phone number, or
its LID when the store has no number, read from the store like
GetAccountStatus does, so a stopped account still has it. Unset while the
account has never paired, which is always the case for CreateAccount.

messages.name: AccountRef
messages.comment:
How a client names an account: the core's canonical UUID, or the optional
client-supplied external reference.

messages.name: AccountSettingUpdate
messages.comment:
An account-wide setting changed on a linked device (#149). One event for
every setting, each its own case.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: mutation time (ms)

fields.name: action_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the mutation's own time (ms); unset when it carried none

messages.name: AddRequestInfo
messages.comment:
V4 invite token the server attaches to a participant that a privacy setting
blocked from a direct add (error "403"). The edge composes the fallback
(send a GroupInviteMessage); the core only relays the token.

fields.name: options
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: in the order the poll offered them

fields.name: votes
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
The edge holds these, not the core. ORDER IS THE CONTRACT: oldest first.
Last vote wins, so a shuffled list tallies a stale answer. The core does
not sort (it has no clock of its own to sort by, and picking one would be
policy) -- it relays the order it was given.

messages.name: AppStateSyncFailedInfo
messages.comment:
An app-state sync ended without every collection synced. Collections cross by
their wire names (`critical_block`, `regular_high`, ...), as the library keeps
them.

fields.name: fatal
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: refused by the server; repeating gets the same answer

fields.name: retryable
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: a later attempt can sync them

fields.name: skipped
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: another writer held them, so this sync did nothing

fields.name: connected
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the client still announced the connection as up

fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The chat the mutation applies to (for a star, the chat that holds the
message).

fields.name: timestamp

When the mutation was made (ms). Falls back to the epoch or the dispatch
time when the mutation carried none: `action_timestamp` tells them apart.

fields.name: action_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
The instant the mutation itself carried (ms); unset when it carried none
(upstream #1562).

fields.label: singular
fields.comment: replayed by a full app-state sync

fields.name: archived
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true=archive, false=unarchive

messages.name: BlocklistEntry
messages.comment: One blocked contact, as the server lists it (#197).

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: The server's `t`, unix seconds. Unset when the server sent none.

fields.name: timezone
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: IANA name, e.g. "America/Sao_Paulo"

fields.name: business_config
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: One entry per opening range: a day with two ranges is two entries.

fields.name: day_of_week_raw
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The server's token, only when `day_of_week` is UNKNOWN.

fields.name: mode_raw

fields.comment: The server's token, only when `mode` is UNKNOWN.

fields.label: optional
fields.comment: minutes past local midnight

fields.name: close_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: minutes past local midnight

messages.name: BusinessProfile
messages.comment:
A business profile, every field the library parses (#132). Names follow the
library's.

fields.name: description
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: "" when the profile has none: the library's own default

fields.name: profile
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Unset when the jid has no business profile (the library answers `None`).

fields.name: expiration_date
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms (the stanza sends seconds)

fields.name: creation_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

messages.name: ButtonReply
messages.comment: Answers a `buttonsMessage`.

fields.name: selected_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: buttonsResponseMessage.selectedButtonId

fields.name: display_text
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: selectedDisplayText

messages.name: CallAcceptance
messages.comment: `<preaccept>` and `<accept>`: the same shape, so one message (#133 rule).

messages.name: CallAudioCodec
messages.comment: One audio codec a device offers or accepts.

fields.name: enc
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: "opus" in every capture

fields.name: rate
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Hz

messages.name: CallEvent
messages.comment:
Inbound `<call>` signaling stanza (lib `IncomingCall`). The core relays the
primitive; the edge composes any ring/answer policy. `call_id` is the
CallAction's id, distinct from `stanza_id`. #135: every field of the
library's struct, and the action as a oneof (payloads in call.proto), whose
case names the action.

fields.name: participant
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Companion-routing metadata copied from the `<call>` wrapper; unset when absent.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: ms (the stanza's `t`, unix seconds)

fields.name: offline
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
An offline-queue replay. The library surfaces a replayed offer as a
MissedCall instead, so here it marks the other actions.

fields.name: caller_username
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: an offer's `username`

fields.name: video_orientation
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: Camera rotation (quarter turns, 0..3) an offer or an accept announced.

fields.name: group
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the group snapshot an offer carried

fields.name: raise_hand
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: wire tag "user_action"

fields.name: unknown_action
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The wire tag of a call action the library added after this core.

fields.name: missed
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
#151: a call that must not ring, surfaced instead of an offer. Today an
offer replayed from the offline queue (`offline` is then true).

messages.name: CallLogHistory
messages.comment:
One call-log record from a history sync (#215): calls the primary device
made or took before this companion was paired. The record fields are the
ones `CallLogUpdate` carries, mapped the same way; the identity fields differ
because a history record has no mutation index:
- `call_id` and `call_creator` come from the record itself. `call_creator` is
  unset when the record named none or one the library could not parse.
- `from_me` is unset when the creator is unknown or this account's own
  identity was not available, never a guess from the record's `isIncoming`.
There is no mutation time: `start_time` is when the call happened.

fields.name: sync_type
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the history notification's sync type

fields.name: chunk_order
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the history chunk's order, when the phone sent one

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: seconds, verbatim

fields.name: start_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms; the server sends seconds

fields.name: group
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: set on a group call

messages.name: CallLogParticipant
messages.comment:
One other party of the call and how the call ended for them. An entry with
no jid is skipped.

messages.name: CallLogUpdate
messages.comment:
One entry of the primary device's call log, synced through app state
(`wa.SyncActionValue.CallLogAction`, #153). The only channel that shows a
call placed on the phone: such a call puts no signalling on this socket, so
CallEvent never sees it. Measured on 2026-10-08: only the companion of the
account that placed the call received one.

Left out on purpose: the record's `isIncoming`, which the library documents
as inverted in mutations WA Web wrote and literal in ones the phone wrote
(read `from_me`), and the record's `callId` / `callCreatorJid`, which repeat
the mutation's index below.

fields.name: call_creator
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: who started the call, from the mutation's index

fields.name: call_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: from the mutation's index

fields.name: from_me
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: this account placed the call (creator compared to this account)

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
When the mutation was written (ms), not when the call happened: that is
`start_time`.

fields.name: from_full_sync
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: replayed by a full app-state sync

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: Seconds, verbatim (measured: 31 for a call the phone showed as 30-31 s).

fields.name: start_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms; the server sends seconds

fields.name: group
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: set on a group call

messages.name: CallMissed
messages.comment: Why a call surfaced as missed rather than ringing (#151).

messages.name: CallOffer
messages.comment: `<offer>`: a call ringing this account.

fields.name: caller_pn
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: unset when the offer carried none

fields.name: group_jid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: set on a group call

messages.name: CallOfferNotice
messages.comment: `<offer_notice>`: a group call announced to its members.

messages.name: CallRaiseHand
messages.comment: `<user_action>`: one participant raised or lowered a hand.

messages.name: CallRejection
messages.comment:
`<reject>`. `reason` absent is the user declining; "busy" and "enc" speak
for one device only (the library's note), the others keep ringing.

messages.name: CallScreenShare
messages.comment: `<screen_share>`: one participant's screen-share state.

messages.name: CallTermination
messages.comment:
`<terminate>`. `reason` as the server sent it ("accepted_elsewhere",
"rejected_elsewhere", "timeout", ...). The durations cross verbatim: their
unit is not verified (a linked device is dismissed before the call ends, so
no live capture carries one, and the library does not document it).

messages.name: CallTransport
messages.comment: `<transport>`: ICE/relay candidate exchange.

messages.name: CallVideoState
messages.comment: `<video state=N>`: the audio/video upgrade handshake.

fields.name: state_code
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The server's number, only when `state` is UNKNOWN (#126 rule).

fields.name: orientation
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: quarter turns, 0..3

fields.name: dec
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: codecs the sender decodes, e.g. "H264,AV1"

messages.name: CallWaitingRoom
messages.comment: `<waiting_room_update>`: admission state of a call-link call.

messages.name: ClearChatChange
messages.comment: The chat's messages were cleared, the chat itself kept.

fields.name: delete_starred

fields.name: delete_media
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: from the mutation's index, not its action

fields.comment: The messages the clear covers (seconds on the wire, as measured, so ms here).

messages.comment:
The server set or withdrew a retirement deadline for this client build.

false (default) = skip the phone's history dump (relay-pure default).

The server refused the connection for a reason that is not a logout, a ban

arrives as ConnectionStateChanged.

Another session took this one over (409, or `conflict type="replaced"`).

the library parsed. Times are ms; the server sends seconds.

linked device).

messages.comment: The server asks for a full contact re-sync (`<sync>`).

messages.comment: A contact edited on a linked device (the `contact` sync action).

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
When the mutation was made (ms). Falls back to the epoch or the dispatch
time when the mutation carried none: `action_timestamp` tells them apart.

fields.name: action_timestamp

fields.comment:
The instant the mutation itself carried (ms); unset when it carried none
(upstream #1562).

fields.name: action
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Unset when `removed` is true: a removal carries no action.

fields.name: removed
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
#153: true when the contact was deleted on a linked device (the syncd
`Remove` of the same `contact` mutation).

messages.name: CreateNewsletterRequest
messages.comment:
Create a channel this account owns (#199). An empty `name` is refused before
the server: a channel without one never exists. `description` goes out as
given when set, absent when not.

fields.name: delete_media
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: from the mutation's index, not its action

fields.name: message_range
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The messages the deletion covers; WA Web deletes by this range.

messages.name: DeleteMessageForMeChange
messages.comment:
One message was deleted for this account only. `AppStateUpdate.chat` is
the chat that holds it.

fields.name: participant
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The sender, for someone else's message in a group; unset for your own
message or in a direct chat.

fields.name: message_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
When the deleted message was sent, in ms. The server sends seconds
(measured: the message's own time, seconds before the mutation).

fields.name: for_everyone
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
true=revoke for all, false=delete for me. A status (`chat` =
`status@broadcast`) cannot be revoked here: that is RevokeStatus, which
needs the recipient list this request has no field for (issue #41).

fields.name: key_index
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: add and remove carry it

fields.name: contact_hash
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: update carries it

messages.name: DeviceNotice
messages.comment:
Someone's devices or identity key changed (#151). The library has already
cleared the sessions and sender keys it had to; this is notice.

messages.name: DisappearingModeChange
messages.comment:
A contact's default disappearing-messages timer changed. Apply it only when
`setting_timestamp` is newer than what you hold.

fields.name: jid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the contact (the library's `from`)

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: 0 = off, 86400 = 24 h (measured)

messages.name: Empty
messages.comment: Empty reply (kept local so the contract needs no well-known-types import).

fields.name: account_uuid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Stays a string (#122): it is not a jid, and no other uuid in the contract
is a message (`AccountRef.uuid`, `Account.uuid`), so a wrapper here would
be the one uuid shaped differently from the rest.

fields.name: monotonic_seq
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Per account, a stream delivers envelopes in strictly increasing
monotonic_seq, which is the order the library dispatched the events in
(the replay, then live, with no repeat between them). A subscriber may
treat a seq at or below the highest it accepted as a duplicate. The only
exceptions are the gap markers (seq -1). There is no order across
accounts. During an offline drain the library processes independent chats
in parallel (up to 8 at once, one per core by default), so in that phase
the order is guaranteed within a chat but not across chats. The sequence
lives in the daemon's memory: it starts again at 0 when the daemon
restarts, so a subscriber that keeps its highest seq across a restart must
reset it when the stream ends (#213).

messages.name: FavoriteStickerChange
messages.comment: A sticker was favorited (`is_favorite` true) or unfavorited (false).

fields.name: media
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
What DownloadMedia takes, with `media_type` STICKER. `file_sha256` is
`StickerUpdate.filehash` decoded: the library checks the decrypted bytes
against it, and the mutation carries it nowhere else (measured: empty, the
download is refused; decoded, it succeeds). Empty when the filehash is not
a base64 SHA-256. Unset when the mutation has no `direct_path`.
`file_length` crosses as sent (measured: 0 on one, 1244 on another).

messages.name: FavoritesChanged
messages.comment:
The account's favorite chats changed on a linked device (the `favorites`
syncd mutation, upstream #1544, issue #48).

Not an AppStateUpdate: favorites is ONE list for the whole account, and each
event carries the whole of it. It REPLACES whatever the consumer held before;
an empty `chats` means no favorites, not "nothing changed". The core relays
each list and keeps none, so replacing is the consumer's job.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: mutation time (ms)

fields.name: from_full_sync
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true when replayed by a full app-state sync

fields.name: raw
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the serialized `wa.SyncActionValue.FavoritesAction`

messages.name: FetchMessageHistoryRequest
messages.comment:
On-demand history fetch (PDO HistorySyncOnDemand): asks the phone for `count`
messages OLDER than the anchor message the edge already has. The answer
arrives asynchronously on the event stream as HistorySyncEvent(s) whose
session_id matches the response below. Requires a live connection.

fields.name: oldest_msg_id

messages.comment:
The shared relay of a group snapshot. Its keys and tokens are private to the

One address of the shared group relay. The raw address bytes are private to

A transaction-ordered group-call snapshot: the `group_update` action, and

The owner of subgroup suggestions moved to a new number. The old owner is

The group as the `<create>` notification carries it, parsed by the library's
group parser (the same one GetGroupMetadata uses). A member who is re-added
receives a `create` too. Unset when the node holds no `<group>` the parser

fields.comment:
The whole `<create>` element (#146), `metadata` included. It carries what
the typed metadata does not: a subgroup's `<linked_parent>`, `<general_chat>`,

messages.name: GroupCreatedMembershipRequests

Group-level disappearing-messages timer. Distinct from the per-message
ephemeral flag carried on SendText/SendMedia; 0 disables.

messages.name: GroupEphemeralSettings

messages.name: GroupInviteJoin

fields.label: singular

Set by JoinWithInvite only (#96); CreateGroup leaves it UNSPECIFIED. `group`
is the same in both outcomes, so this is the only way to tell a join from
a request that waits for an admin.

messages.name: GroupLinked
messages.comment:
A subgroup was linked to a community. `link_type` is the typed attribute
(`sub_group` for the community's notification, `sibling_group` for the other
subgroups'). The linked groups are the `<group jid subject s_t/>` children of

fields.name: stanza
fields.label: singular

messages.name: GroupLockedChange
messages.comment: Only admins may edit the group info now.

fields.label: singular

Parsed with the library's own exact match. UNSPECIFIED when the node had
no content.

fields.name: mode_raw

messages.name: GroupMemberAddModeRequest
messages.comment:
Who may add members (#198). The same enum GetGroupMetadata reports, so the
edge writes what it reads; UNSPECIFIED and UNKNOWN name no setting and are
refused with InvalidArgument before anything reaches the server.

Who may share the group's history with a new member (#198). Refused like
GroupMemberAddModeRequest.

messages.name: GroupMembershipApprovalRequest
messages.comment: Someone asked to join. The requester is `GroupUpdate.participant`.

fields.name: parent_group

messages.name: GroupMetadata
messages.comment:
A group as the library hands it over, every field of whatsapp-rust's
`GroupMetadata` (#132).

Rules for every message in this file:
- A field the library leaves out is unset, never 0 or "": `optional` on a
  scalar, an unset message for a `Jid` or a sub-message, UNSPECIFIED for an
  enum.
- A point in time is `int64` milliseconds, like every timestamp in this
  contract; the server counts these in seconds, and the core converts.
  A value whose unit is not verified crosses verbatim as `uint64`, and its
  comment says so.

fields.name: addressing_mode
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Which namespace the roster is addressed in, so the edge knows whether a
participant `jid` is a `@lid` before it tries to name anyone (#1).

fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

fields.name: subject_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

fields.label: optional

fields.comment: As the server sent it: the unit is not verified, so it is not converted.

messages.comment:
A member as a group notification names them. Not `GroupParticipant`: the
notification carries a different set (a server-rendered `display_name`,
`join_time` and the history state at the top level, no label).

fields.name: display_name
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
The server's label, e.g. "+55∙∙∙∙∙∙∙∙∙79" when the member is not in the
contacts of whoever caused the notification.

fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The server's `participant` is GROUP_PARTICIPANT_TYPE_MEMBER: the same role
GroupMetadata names `member`. The library reads a missing or unknown type
as `participant`; UNSPECIFIED only on a join request's entries
(`created_membership_requests`), which carry no type at all.

fields.name: join_time
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

messages.name: GroupParticipant
messages.comment:
One member, whole (#1): the jid the group addresses them by, and the phone
jid and lid the server sent beside it. In a LID-addressed group `jid` is a
`@lid` and `phone_number` is the only phone the roster carries.

fields.name: username
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
The roster is one of the few places the server volunteers a username at
all (a received message never carries one).

fields.name: details
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Unset when the roster entry carried none of these attributes.

fields.name: participant_label_mtime

fields.comment: As the server sent it: the unit is not verified, so it is not converted.

add, remove, promote, demote, modify, linked_group_promote and

A member suggested a group for the community (#146). The suggestion is

As the server sent it: whether it is a deadline or a duration, and in

messages.name: HistorySyncEvent
messages.comment:
History-sync chunk, only emitted when the account connected with backfill
enabled (ConnectAccountRequest.backfill_history) or in answer to
FetchMessageHistory. The core relays the blob verbatim: the edge decodes
`raw` (a `wa.HistorySync` protobuf) itself. Delivered in chunks.

fields.name: sync_type
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: wa.HistorySync.HistorySyncType (InitialBootstrap|Recent|PushName|OnDemand|...)

fields.name: session_id
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: Set for on-demand syncs: correlate with FetchMessageHistoryResponse.session_id.

fields.name: raw
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: decompressed `wa.HistorySync` protobuf

fields.name: implicit
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
True when the library noticed it while decrypting, false when the server
sent `<identity/>`.

messages.name: InboundMessage
messages.comment:
A message in a chat. Almost always one WhatsApp delivered -- but ALSO the
echo of a message this relay itself sent, with `key.from_me` true.

Issue #22: WhatsApp echoes a send to every device on the account except the
one that sent it. The relay holds ONE device session per account and every
consumer of the socket shares it, so a send made through MessagingService
comes from our own device and nothing comes back -- not live, not on the next
history read. Only the consumer that made the call ever learned the message
existed, while its receipts reached everyone, naming an id nobody had. So the
relay publishes the echo its own shape prevents. It is the only MESSAGE on
this bus that WhatsApp did not produce (the other events the core makes up
are the `raw` `gap` and `subscription_gap` markers of EventService).

It goes to EVERY subscriber, the caller included: excluding the caller would
mean the bus knowing who called, and the core has no notion of client
identity. Drop the duplicate on `key.id`, which a consumer must handle
anyway, since a replayed event has to land on the same row.

WHICH SENDS ECHO: every one that puts a message in a chat. SendText,
SendMedia, SendReaction, SendContact, SendInteractiveReply, SendPoll,
SendPollVote, EditMessage, DeleteMessage with `for_everyone`, PostStatusText,
PostStatusMedia and RevokeStatus. DeleteMessage for-me sends nothing to the chat (it is an
app-state mutation), so it has nothing to echo, and neither does
NewsletterService.SendNewsletterPollVote: a channel vote is an add-on on a
message, not a message in the channel (issue #26). The payload is always the
message the send encoded, handed back by the library (upstream #1406), never
a reconstruction -- including the half the library builds itself (issue #38):

  - EditMessage / DeleteMessage echo their protocol message: `is_edit` or
    `is_delete`, `protocol_target` naming the edited/revoked message, and
    `key.id` the edit/revoke stanza's own id, same as the edit another device
    of the account receives.
  - SendPollVote echoes the encrypted vote (`pollUpdateMessage`), so `text`
    is empty and the vote is read from `raw_message` with the poll's secret,
    like any vote that arrives.
  - PostStatus* echo with `chat` = `status@broadcast`, and so does
    RevokeStatus, as a delete (`is_delete`) whose `protocol_target` is the
    status.

One caveat on SendInteractiveReply (issue #28). An interactive reply echoes
with its `raw_message` whole — every id, label and the quoted offer — but
`text` comes back EMPTY, because `project_content` has no case for
`buttonsResponseMessage` / `listResponseMessage` /
`templateButtonReplyMessage` / `interactiveResponseMessage`. This is not
specific to the echo: an inbound reply from the other side projects the same
way today. A consumer that mirrors a conversation off `text` alone will show
a blank row where a tap happened, and must read `raw_message` for these.
Written down rather than papered over, because the display text IS in the
payload and looking blank is the kind of gap that reads as a delivery bug.

The echo's `raw_message` is that payload AS THE SEND ENCODED IT, which is not
byte-identical to what the recipient decrypts. The library's send path hoists
a `messageContextInfo` (device-list metadata) into the encoded message when
the message carries none, so the recipient's copy is larger. Measured
2026-09-03 on one text across both accounts of one relay: 30 bytes here, 69
on the receiving side, same message id. Everything a consumer decodes the
payload FOR -- text, media descriptors, poll options, sticker metadata -- is
identical; only the wire envelope the library adds per recipient is not.

`chat` likewise names the conversation from THIS account's side: the echo
carries the jid the send was addressed to, while the recipient's own event
may name the same conversation by its `@lid` form. Neither is rewritten.

fields.name: sender
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Unset on an echo when the account has no jid of its own yet, and on a
channel-history row, which names no sender.

fields.name: media
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: set for media messages

fields.name: reaction
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: set for reaction messages

fields.name: protocol_target
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Set on an inbound edit (is_edit) or revoke (is_delete): the key of the
message the protocol action targets (the edited/revoked message). It lives
in the lib's protocol_message.key, distinct from this event's own key
(which is the edit/revoke stanza id). For an edit, `text` carries the new
text; a new-style E2E edit arrives un-decrypted (is_edit set, text empty).

fields.name: sender_alt
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The other-namespace form of the two ends, verbatim from the stanza: when
`sender` is a `@lid`, `sender_alt` is the phone jid the stanza carried (and
the reverse for a phone sender); `recipient_alt` is the same for the other
end of a DM. Unset when the stanza carried none -- the core relays these,
it never looks them up (that is ContactService.ResolveLidPn) and never
guesses. This is what makes a `@lid` chat identifiable with no round trip
(issue #1).

fields.name: sticker_pack
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Set for a sticker PACK message (issue #58). `media` then carries the pack's
archive under MEDIA_TYPE_STICKER_PACK; this says what is inside it and
carries the thumbnail's own descriptor.

fields.name: raw_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: serialized wa.Message for advanced consumers

fields.name: sticker_audio
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The clip of a sound sticker (issue #278), set only when the sticker carries
one; `media` stays the sticker image. MEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO, so DownloadMedia
fetches it like any audio. The format is whatever the sender uploaded
(Ogg/Opus from the official apps); the core does not inspect it.

messages.name: Jid
messages.comment:
A WhatsApp JID, e.g. "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net" or a group/lid jid.
Every field that carries a jid is this message, never a bare string (#72).
In a request it is parsed: unset or an empty value is InvalidArgument
"missing jid" where the field is required, absence where it is optional.
In a response or an event it carries the value the core has, verbatim, and
a jid the core does not have is an unset field, never an empty value.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: ms (measured in seconds on the wire)

fields.name: signed_bytes
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the signed key index list, on add

messages.name: LabelChatAssociation
messages.comment: A label was put on (`labeled` true) or taken off a chat.

messages.name: LabelEdit
messages.comment:
A label was created, edited or deleted. In the consumer app a label is a
chat list ("Lists"), measured live 2026-10-08 as `list_type` CUSTOM.
Deleting sends `deleted` true with an empty name and `is_active` false.

fields.name: color
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the app's palette index, verbatim

fields.name: predefined_id
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: set on the app's ready-made lists

fields.name: mute_end_time_ms
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms, as its name says (always 0 when measured)

messages.name: LabelMessageAssociation
messages.comment:
A label was put on or taken off one message. Not measured: the app no
longer labels messages.

messages.name: LabelSublistUpdate
messages.comment:
One entry of a label's sublist changed on a linked device (#215): the entry
keyed by `(predefined_id, chat)`. Apply it as an upsert or a removal of that
key; delivery is not exactly once, and nothing synthesizes a removal when the
parent label goes away. `predefined_id` is in `LabelEdit.predefined_id`'s
namespace: it is neither a label id nor a list type.

fields.name: chat
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: PN or LID, as the mutation named it

fields.name: action_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
The mutation's own time (ms); unset when it carried none or one out of
range. Zero is a time, not "absent".

fields.name: from_full_sync
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: replayed by a full app-state sync

fields.name: upsert_sub_list_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the entry's new sublist id; 0 is a value

fields.name: remove
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the wire does not carry the old sublist id

messages.name: LabelUpdate
messages.comment:
A label (a chat list, in the consumer app) changed on a linked device
(#149). The label belongs to the account, so it is not an AppStateUpdate.

fields.name: label_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the mutation's index key, not a jid

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: mutation time (ms)

fields.name: from_full_sync
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true when replayed by a full app-state sync

messages.name: LidPnMapping
messages.comment:
One LID <-> phone-number pair, exactly as the library learned it. Both sides
render as full JIDs ("<user>@lid" / "<user>@s.whatsapp.net"): the store keeps
only the user parts, and each side's namespace is fixed by definition. A side
the store has no user part for comes back unset, never a bare "@lid".

fields.label: singular

The library's own tag for how it learned the pair, verbatim:
usync|pairing|peer_pn_message|peer_lid_message|recipient_latest_lid|
migration_sync_latest|migration_sync_old|blocklist_active|
blocklist_inactive|device_notification|other.

messages.comment:
One answer per requested jid, in request order. `query` is the requested
jid exactly as it was sent: a `@c.us` query comes back `@c.us`.

fields.name: mapping
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: unset when found=false

messages.name: LinkPreview
messages.comment:
Link-preview card for an outgoing text. The EDGE fetches the URL and
supplies every field here; the core relays them verbatim and performs no
outbound HTTP (same doctrine as media: fetch policy and the SSRF surface
belong to the edge). Note: this waproto has no canonical_url field, so
matched_text doubles as the URL the preview belongs to.

fields.name: preview_type
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Numeric wa ExtendedTextMessage.PreviewType (0=NONE, 1=VIDEO, ...).
0 is the proto3 default and is relayed as "field absent".

messages.name: LinkPreviewsSetting

messages.name: ListReply
messages.comment:
Answers a `listMessage`. `title` and `description` are the chosen ROW's, and
the official client sends both (4 of 4) -- they are what the conversation
shows, while `selected_row_id` is what the bot matches on.

fields.name: selected_row_id

messages.name: LockChange

The server's numeric code, only when `reason` is UNKNOWN (a code the
library does not name). 0 otherwise.

fields.name: logout_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The server's own copy for this logout, when it sent any (in practice on
an account lock). Unset otherwise (#134).

fields.name: on_connect

True when the server refused the connection itself (a `<failure>`), false
for a logout that came later (a `<stream:error>`, or a local logout).

The whole stanza that caused the logout (#138): a `<failure>` when
`on_connect` is true, a `<stream:error>` otherwise. An account lock puts
its one-time `appeal_token` here, which nothing else carries. Unset for a
local logout, which received nothing.

messages.comment:
Localized text the server wants shown on a forced logout (`<failure>`'s
logout_message_header / _subtext). WA Web shows it only when `locale`
equals the client's own, and falls back to generic copy otherwise; the
locale travels with the text so a consumer can apply the same rule.

fields.name: read

Used by MarkRead (the receipt), MarkChatRead and MarkUnread (the app-state

state is per chat, not per message.

The messages being acknowledged. Empty acknowledges nothing and the
library returns without emitting a stanza, so a caller with nothing to say
costs nothing.

The message's author. Required for a group read: a receipt names whose
messages are being acknowledged. Absent in a DM, where the chat is the
author.
