messages.comment:
`<notification type="mex">` (#151): a server GraphQL update, routed by
`op_name`. `payload_json` is the SERVER's JSON body, not the library's
shape: the library parses it and the core writes it back out, so keys come
sorted and the content is the same. Decode it by `op_name`.

fields.name: offline
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: set on a backlog replay (often a timestamp, as the server sends it)

fields.name: mute_end_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
When the mute ends, in ms as the server sent it (measured live
2026-10-07: an 8 h mute ended at the mute time + 28 800 000). Unset on an
unmute.

fields.name: mute_everyone_mention_end_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: As the server sent it: always 0 when measured, so its unit is not verified.

fields.name: muted
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: false=unmute (mute_until_ms ignored)

fields.name: mute_until_ms
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
0 with muted=true means mute indefinitely; otherwise a future epoch-ms.
The lib rejects a non-future timestamp; the core relays that error and the
edge supplies a valid one (the core tracks no clock policy).

messages.name: NativeFlowReply
messages.comment:
Answers an `interactiveMessage` (native flow).

Built from the proto, NOT from a capture: the store held 13 interactive
offers and no reply to one, so unlike the three above nothing here is
confirmed against traffic the official client produced.

fields.name: name
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: nativeFlowResponseMessage.name

fields.name: params_json
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: nativeFlowResponseMessage.paramsJson

fields.name: body_text
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: interactiveResponseMessage.body.text

fields.name: version
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: 0 leaves the field absent, which is the proto default of 1.

messages.name: Newsletter
messages.comment:
A channel (`@newsletter`), relayed as the server describes it.

Issue #6: a consumer that materialises conversations from the event stream
could otherwise address these rows only by jid. Nothing here is derived or
guessed — an inbound newsletter message carries an empty `push_name` and a
`sender` equal to the newsletter jid, and history sync brings no name either,
so this is the only place the name exists.

fields.name: description
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Absent fields relay as the proto3 default, never a placeholder, except
`state` and `verification` below.

fields.name: verification
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
When the server omits it this reads UNVERIFIED, the library's default
(#56): UNSPECIFIED is never emitted. A value the library does not model
is UNKNOWN, with the server's spelling verbatim in `verification_raw`.

fields.name: state
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
When the server omits it this reads ACTIVE (#56): UNSPECIFIED is never
emitted. Another server token (a deleted channel reads `DELETED`) is
UNKNOWN, verbatim in `state_raw`.

fields.name: role
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
This account's role in the channel. UNSPECIFIED when the server says
nothing or names a role the library drops (#56); no raw field, because
the library hands no token over.

fields.name: creation_time
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: Unix seconds, 0 when the server omits it.

messages.name: NewsletterLiveUpdate
messages.comment:
A channel's tallies, pushed while this account is subscribed to it
(NewsletterService.SubscribeNewsletterLiveUpdates, upstream #1554, issue
#26).

Measured live 2026-09-25 on the WhatsApp channel: the first push after
subscribing held the 10 latest messages, the next one (30 s later) only the
two whose counts had changed. So a message missing from a push is unchanged,
not zeroed. Counts are across every follower, the same numbers the history
page carries.

fields.name: votes
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: Per-option tallies, on a poll only. Same hash as NewsletterMessage.votes.

fields.name: forwards_count
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
Absent when the server sent no `<forwards_count>`, which is not a count of
zero. (Every message in the measured pushes carried one.)

messages.name: NewsletterMessage
messages.comment: One row of a channel's history, as `<messages>` returned it (issue #26).

fields.name: message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The message itself, in the SAME shape the event bus delivers. A channel
message is plaintext on the wire (no Signal E2E), so the `<plaintext>`
bytes decode to the very `wa.Message` a live event carries, and it goes
through the same projection: one concept, one shape, one decoder on the
edge.

What a history row cannot fill stays at the proto3 default rather than
gaining a placeholder: the node carries no sender, no push_name and no
alt-namespace jids. `key.from_me` is the ONLY sender information it has
(the server's `is_sender`), and `key.chat`/`chat` are the jid the
caller asked for, not something read off the node.

`timestamp` is milliseconds, like every other timestamp in this contract.
The stanza counts in seconds; the conversion happens in the core so the
edge never has two units for one field.

fields.name: server_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Server-assigned and monotonic. This is the pagination cursor (`before`),
and the key the server's own side-channel add-ons hang off — a channel
reaction is addressed by `server_id`, not by the message id. Distinct from
`message.key.id`, which is what edit/revoke key on.

fields.name: votes
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
The poll tally, on a POLL row. Empty everywhere else, and empty on a poll
nobody has voted in.

fields.name: forwards_count
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
How many times the channel's subscribers forwarded this row. 0 when the
server omits the node.

fields.name: original_timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
When a touched row was first posted and last edited (#51), read off
`<meta original_msg_t>` and `<meta msg_edit_t>`. The server counts the
first in seconds and the second in milliseconds, in the same node; both
cross here in milliseconds, like every timestamp in this contract. 0 when
the attribute is absent.

Measured live 2026-09-25 (two channels, 200 rows): an edited row
(ADMIN_EDIT, "3") carries both, a revoked one (ADMIN_REVOKE, "8") only the
original, an untouched one neither. On an edited row `message.timestamp` is the EDIT
time, so `original_timestamp` is the only place the posting time survives.

messages.name: NewsletterMuteRequest
messages.comment:
Mute or unmute a followed channel (#199): the "Mute" a follower toggles in
the app, the channel's own updates (MUTE_ADMIN_ACTIVITY).

messages.name: NewsletterMyAddOns
messages.comment:
One message's add-ons. Each is absent when this account has none on it, so
an absent `poll_vote` (never voted) is not the same as one with no hashes
(vote removed).

fields.name: messages
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
Only messages this account has an add-on on (the library's reading of the
answer). Measured once: with limit 20, only the one poll voted on came back.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
ms. The server's `t` for the last vote sent, equal to that vote's ack `t`
(3 of 3 measured).

fields.name: option_hashes
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
The selection the server holds, 32 bytes each. EMPTY after the vote was
removed: the server keeps a removal as a dated, empty selection.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: ms

messages.name: NewsletterPollVote
messages.comment:
One option's tally in a channel poll, straight off `<votes><vote/></votes>`.

The option is named by HASH, never by text: 32 bytes, the SHA-256 of the
option name exactly as the poll's payload spells it. Match it against
`sha256(option_name)` over the options in the poll's own `raw_message`.

This is why a channel poll needs no `message_secret` and why voting in one
does not fit `SendPollVote` (issue #26): the vote is by hash, in the clear,
and the server does the counting. Measured live 2026-09-21: 4 `<vote>` nodes
for a 4-option channel poll, 32 bytes of content each. Vote with
`NewsletterService.SendNewsletterPollVote`, naming options by this same hash.

A `<vote>` that could not fill both fields is skipped, not relayed (#43):
content that is not 32 bytes names no option, and a vote with no `count`
(or one that is not a number) is not a vote for nobody. So an option absent
from `votes` means the server gave no tally for it that the core could read,
NOT that its count is zero.

fields.name: option_hash
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: 32 bytes, SHA-256 of the option name

messages.name: NewsletterReactionCount
messages.comment:
How many viewers reacted with one emoji, as the server tallies it.

This is a COUNT, not a list: a channel has no participant roster the viewer
can see, so nobody's identity crosses here. It is also the only tally the
server volunteers per message.

fields.name: code
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the emoji, spelled as the server sent it

messages.name: NumberChange
messages.comment: A contact changed their phone number (`<modify>`).

fields.name: old_lid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: unset when the server sent none

messages.name: OfflineSyncCompleted
messages.comment:
How many the drain actually delivered.

Issue #11: this is dispatched only when the drain finishes. A resume whose
connection ends mid-drain never gets one; OfflineSyncInterrupted arrives in
its place.

A missing completion means "not caught up yet", never "lost" (upstream
oxidezap/whatsapp-rust#1380). Offline stanzas are only confirmed by the
aggregate receipt flush that a COMPLETED drain performs, and teardown drops
that buffer, so nothing in an interrupted drain is acked and the server
redelivers all of it on the next connection.

The library (upstream #1380, pinned by #30) does not answer with silence:
an armed resume whose connection ends emits OfflineSyncInterrupted, and the
client holds WA Web's own 60s stanza-inactivity timer, so a drain that stalls
on a LIVE connection finishes itself.

The core puts no deadline on the wait. How long a missing completion may
stay missing is edge policy, same as a missing ack. Upstream agrees on where
that timer belongs, which is inside the client.

messages.name: OfflineSyncInterrupted
messages.comment:
A resume that did NOT finish: its connection ended mid-drain (issue #38,
upstream oxidezap/whatsapp-rust#1380). Emitted once per armed resume, in
place of the OfflineSyncCompleted it will never get.

It means "not caught up, the remainder comes back", never "lost": the drain
acked nothing, so the server redelivers all of it and a fresh
OfflineSyncPreview announces it on the next connection. `delivered` is what
reached this stream before the cut; those events may arrive again with the
redelivery. Both numbers are the server's, so read them as a progress report,
not an invariant.

fields.name: total
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: what the preview announced for this drain

fields.name: delivered
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: offline stanzas processed before the connection ended

messages.name: OfflineSyncPreview
messages.comment:
What the server says it is holding for this account when a connection comes
back up, from the `offline_preview` node. `total` is authoritative; the
per-kind counts need not sum to it.

Issue #11: this is the first half of the signal that a reconnect owes this
account a backlog. Compare `total` here with `count` on the
OfflineSyncCompleted that should follow.

fields.name: backfill_history
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: see PairWithQrRequest.backfill_history

fields.name: backfill_history
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
true = connect with history backfill ON so the InitialBootstrap dump the
phone pushes right after linking is emitted as HistorySyncEvent(s).

fields.name: business_name
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: empty for personal (non-business) accounts

fields.name: lid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the account's LID (hidden-PN) identity

fields.name: platform
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: e.g. "android", "smba", "iphone"

messages.name: PairingCodeErrorInfo
messages.comment: A phone-number pair-code flow failed, so no linking will come of it (#150).

fields.name: rejection
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
UNSPECIFIED when nothing was refused: the failure was local (validation,
no connection) or the request got no answer.

fields.name: rejection_code
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The server's number, only when `rejection` is UNKNOWN (#73 rule).

fields.name: backoff_ms
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: The wait the server asked for, from its `backoff` attribute (ms).

fields.name: detail
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The failure as the library renders it for logs. Do not branch on it.

messages.name: PairingCodeRefreshInfo
messages.comment:
The pair code in progress is no longer valid (#150): the server asked for a
new one, or the phone never answered within a minute. The library has
already cleared the flow, so nothing more comes for this code.

fields.name: force_manual
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the server wants the code requested again explicitly

messages.name: PairingQrCodesExhaustedInfo
messages.comment:
The server's QR refs are used up: no QR is left until a new connection
(#150).

fields.name: disconnected
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
True when the client closed the connection itself, which it does only
with no pair code outstanding. False: a pair code is still valid on this
connection, and the connection stays up.

messages.name: PairingUpdate
messages.comment:
Streamed during pairing: QR refreshes, the pair code, then success or error.
PairWithQr and PairWithCode end after `paired`, `error`, `code_error`,
`code_refresh`, or `qr_codes_exhausted` with `disconnected` true: nothing
more can come on that flow (#150). Asking again is the caller's decision.
The stream also ends with no terminal update when the daemon shuts down
(#247); the caller can ask again once it is back.

messages.name: ParticipantChange
messages.comment:
One server verdict for one participant of a participant-change request. The
server answers per participant, so a request can partially succeed: `error`
empty means that participant went through.

fields.name: phone_number
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The phone jid the roster carries next to a `@lid` participant; unset when
the server sent none.

messages.name: ParticipantsResponse
messages.comment:
Relayed verbatim, one entry per participant the server answered for. The core
does not collapse this into a single ok/failed verdict: which partial failure
is retryable, invitable, or fatal is edge policy.

messages.name: PictureChange
messages.comment: A profile picture set or removed, a user's or a group's.

fields.name: author
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the admin who changed a group's picture; unset for a person's

fields.name: picture_id
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: the server's id; absent on removals, and sometimes on sets

fields.name: pinned
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true=pin, false=unpin

fields.name: undecryptable
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
How many of the supplied votes could not be opened at all: a wrong
message_secret, or a voter in a namespace with no known counterpart. The
library drops those from the tally with nothing but a log line, which from
the edge is indistinguishable from "nobody voted". Same reasoning as the
two offline-sync counts: a silent loss has to be countable.

messages.name: PollVote
messages.comment: One vote as it arrived, straight out of a PollUpdateMessage.

fields.name: thumbnail
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: JPEG preview; the edge generates it (no transcode)

fields.name: seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: video duration; ignored for image

fields.name: background_argb
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: 0xAARRGGBB; 0 is a valid (transparent) value

fields.name: font
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: font style index (0-4 on WhatsApp Web)

fields.name: recipients
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: device set the status is encrypted to

messages.name: PresenceUpdate
messages.comment:
Two library events share this message: real presence (Event::Presence) and a
chat state (Event::ChatPresence). They measure different things, so a field
only one of them can answer is left absent on the other rather than filled
with a literal (issue #24).

fields.name: online
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
Present only on real presence. A chat state does not measure whether the
contact is online, so it carries no value here.

fields.name: chat
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The conversation a chat state happened in: the group jid when somebody is
typing in a group, the contact's own jid in a direct chat. Unset on real
presence, which is not scoped to a conversation. Without it a group
"composing" and a DM "composing" are identical bytes (issue #24).
Relayed verbatim, so in a direct chat it is whichever namespace the stanza
used — measured live on 2026-09-11, that is the sender's `@lid`, equal to
`jid`. The core does not rewrite it onto the phone namespace; resolve it
with ContactService.ResolveLidPn if the edge files chats by number.

messages.name: PreviewInviteRequest
messages.comment: Preview an invite's group metadata without joining.

messages.name: QuickReplyUpdate
messages.comment:
A quick reply was created, edited or deleted on a linked device (#149).
Deleting is the same mutation with `deleted` true and empty texts, not a
removal, so check the flag.

fields.name: id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the mutation's index key

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: mutation time (ms)

messages.name: QuoteContext
messages.comment:
The message a message quotes (#217). `quoted.chat` is the chat the QUOTED
message is in, which is not always the reply's:
- Inbound, it is the context's `remoteJid` when the sender set one (a private
  reply to a group message names the group, a reply to a status names
  `status@broadcast`), else the reply's own chat. Any message type can
  carry a quote, a media reply included.
- On a send, a `quoted.chat` other than `to` goes out as the `remoteJid`, so a
  private reply or a reply to a status can be sent. One equal to `to`, unset
  or empty sends none, as WhatsApp's clients do for a reply in the same chat.
  A value that is not a jid is InvalidArgument.

messages.name: RawEvent
messages.comment:
Catch-all so the edge never silently loses an event type or a broadcast gap.
Reserved kinds (both carry monotonic_seq -1 and an empty payload):
  "gap"              one account's subscriber lagged its broadcast buffer;
                     account_uuid is set: resync it via GetAccountStatus.
  "subscription_gap" the all-accounts created-channel lagged; account_uuid
                     is empty: re-subscribe or reconcile via ListAccounts.
Any other kind is a forward-compat relay of a lib event (payload = JSON).

messages.name: ReachoutTimelockUpdate
messages.comment:
The account's reachout timelock changed (#215): WhatsApp restricting new
conversations this account may start. It reports state, not a policy the core
applies. Every field crosses as the server sent it: `is_active` false is a
lifted restriction, unset makes no claim, and the deadline is the server's
string (its format has not been seen on the wire). The same notification also
arrives right after as a `MexNotification`.

fields.name: offline
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: set on a backlog replay, verbatim

fields.name: type_raw
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The stanza's own `type` attribute, verbatim, only when `type` is UNKNOWN:
the core is a relay and never drops what the server said.

messages.name: RecipientFanout
messages.comment:
The recipient half of a DM send, as the library counted it (upstream #1362).
`SendResult` and the server ack only say the message was taken; this says
which of the recipient's devices got something to decrypt, at send time,
before any `delivered` receipt could arrive.

Four facts, nothing derived: "partial" is `encrypted < addressed`, and what
to do about it (retry, warn, wait for a receipt) is the edge's call. A send
that reached no recipient device at all never answers with this: it fails.

`addressed` counts the recipient's hosted devices too (WhatsApp Business
Coexistence, `@hosted` / `@hosted.lid`), so for such a recipient a failed
hosted device makes `encrypted < addressed`.

All zeros means a self-chat, which has no recipient half. It says nothing
about this account's own devices, so a note to self is NOT settled by it:
that case still has neither a receipt nor a count.

fields.name: addressed
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: recipient devices the fan-out attempted

fields.name: encrypted
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: of those, how many got an <enc>

fields.name: skipped_primary
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: device 0 (the phone) was among the misses

fields.name: had_unregistered_device
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the server answered 406 for at least one

messages.name: RejectCallRequest
messages.comment:
Reject a call ringing this account (#200). The three identifiers are the
ones a `CallEvent` offer carries: `peer` is its `from` (the `<call to>` the
reject goes back to) and `call_creator` its `call_creator`. They stay
separate because companion-device signaling can make them differ.

messages.name: RemoveRecentStickerChange
messages.comment: A sticker was removed from the recent-stickers list.

fields.name: last_sticker_sent_ts
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
When the sticker was last sent, in ms as the server sends it (measured).
WA Web drops its recent entry only when that entry is not newer than
this, and unconditionally when it is unset.

messages.name: RevokeStatusRequest
messages.comment:
Revoke a status this account posted (issue #41). A status revoke is encrypted
to the same device set as the status itself, so the edge hands back the
recipient list it posted with. The core keeps no record of it (relay-pure).

fields.name: message_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the status's own id: PostStatus* SendResult.key.id

fields.name: recipients
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: the same device set the status was posted to

messages.name: SelfPushNameUpdate
messages.comment:
This account's own push name changed (#153), from an app-state
`setting_pushName` mutation, a history sync or an account_sync notification.
Not the retired `PushNameUpdate`, which named a contact and is never emitted.

fields.name: old_name
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: empty when the account had none yet (first sync after pairing)

fields.name: quoted_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The quoted message's own payload, a serialized `wa.Message` (#230): relayed
as `ContextInfo.quotedMessage` with the quote, so a receiver that does not
hold the original still shows what was quoted. Empty sends none. The core
looks nothing up. Bytes with no `quote.quoted` are InvalidArgument, and so
are bytes that are not a `wa.Message`.

fields.name: quote
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The offer being answered. REQUIRED, and InvalidArgument without it: a reply
that names no offer is not a reply. All 10 captured ones quote the offer,
and that is how the bot ties the tap back to what it asked.

fields.name: quoted_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The offer's own payload, verbatim -- the `raw_message` of the event that
delivered it. OPTIONAL, and every captured reply carries it: the official
client embeds the whole offer in `contextInfo.quotedMessage`, not just its
id. The core looks nothing up; it relays this if the edge has it and omits
it if not. Whether a given bot needs it is the bot's business, which is why
this is a field and not a lookup.

fields.name: chunk
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the media itself (the sticker image, for a sound sticker)

fields.name: sticker_audio
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the clip; only after a header with sticker_audio

fields.name: ptt
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Voice note (PTT): ptt=true plus seconds turn an audio into a voice note.
WhatsApp only renders the PTT bubble for OGG/Opus payloads; the edge
supplies the right bytes (the core does not transcode). waveform is the
optional amplitude strip shown in the bubble.

fields.name: ephemeral_seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
0 = not ephemeral; otherwise relayed as ContextInfo.expiration (the edge
supplies the chat's setting, exactly as on SendTextRequest).

fields.name: ptv
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Video note (PTV, the round "instant video"): when media_type is VIDEO and
ptv=true, the built VideoMessage ships as Message.ptv_message instead of
video_message. The edge supplies a square clip; the core does not transcode.

fields.name: quoted_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The quoted message's own payload, a serialized `wa.Message` (#230): relayed
as `ContextInfo.quotedMessage` with the quote, so a receiver that does not
hold the original still shows what was quoted. Empty sends none. The core
looks nothing up. Bytes with no `quote.quoted` are InvalidArgument, and so
are bytes that are not a `wa.Message`.

fields.name: sticker_audio
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
A sound sticker (issue #278): only with media_type STICKER, anything else
is InvalidArgument before the first byte. The clip's bytes follow as
`sticker_audio` parts, in any order with the image's `chunk` parts; a
header with this set and no clip bytes is InvalidArgument. The core does
not transcode: the edge supplies Ogg/Opus. Unset sends a plain sticker.

messages.name: SendNewsletterPollVoteRequest
messages.comment:
Vote in a channel poll (issue #26). A channel is not E2E, so this is not
`SendPollVote`: no `message_secret`, no encryption. Each option is named by
its hash, the same `NewsletterPollVote.option_hash` the tallies use.

Measured live 2026-09-25 on the WhatsApp channel's poll: every send carries
the WHOLE selection and the server keeps exactly the last list, and an empty
list removes the vote. Read the result back with GetMyNewsletterAddOns.

fields.name: jid
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the channel, `...@newsletter`

fields.name: server_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The POLL's server_id (`NewsletterMessage.server_id`), not a new id.

fields.name: option_hashes
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
32 bytes each: sha256 of the option name exactly as the poll payload
spells it (names carry variation selectors and ZWJ; a retyped name hashes
to an option the server does not know). At most 1000, none repeated.
InvalidArgument otherwise, before anything is sent.

fields.name: stanza_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The vote stanza's id. The server's verdict is the ServerAckEvent with this
`id`; no ack for it means the server never took it. There is no echo: a
vote puts no message in the channel.

fields.name: options
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: 2..=12 distinct names (lib validates)

fields.name: selectable_count
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
A chat: 1..=options.len(). A channel (`@newsletter`): 1 for a single
answer or 0 for several, as WA Web publishes them; anything above 1 is
InvalidArgument (#220). The library validates both, and the core relays
the number as given. A channel also refuses a blank name or option.

messages.name: SendPollResult
messages.comment:
message_secret is the per-poll key the edge needs to decrypt incoming votes;
the core hands it back as a primitive and stores nothing (relay-pure). A
channel poll is plaintext and its votes are not encrypted, so it carries no
secret and the field is empty (#220).

fields.name: recipient_fanout
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Same as SendResult.recipient_fanout: a poll to a DM goes through the same
fan-out as any other message (#47).

messages.name: SendPollVoteRequest
messages.comment:
The poll is addressed by (chat, poll_id, poll_creator) rather than by a
MessageKey: the library derives the key's other fields itself (from_me from
the creator, participant from the chat's kind), so a MessageKey here would be
three fields the core ignores. The creator is explicit for the same reason it
is not derived -- guessing an identity is exactly what the core does not do.

fields.name: poll_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: message id of the poll-creation message

fields.name: poll_creator
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: who sent the poll

fields.name: message_secret
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: 32 bytes, from SendPollResult or the payload

fields.name: options
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
Chosen option names, spelled exactly as the poll offered them (a vote
references options by SHA-256 of the name). Empty retracts the vote, and
a second vote replaces the first rather than adding to it.

fields.name: emoji
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: empty string removes the reaction

fields.name: recipient_fanout
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
What a DM's fan-out reached (#47). Absent for every other send: a group, a
status, a delete-for-me that sent nothing. Zeros would read as "addressed
nobody", which is a different fact.

fields.name: ephemeral_seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
0 = not ephemeral; otherwise relayed as ContextInfo.expiration. The edge
supplies the chat's current disappearing-messages setting; the core never
tracks or decides durations.

fields.name: quoted_message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The quoted message's own payload, a serialized `wa.Message` (#230): relayed
as `ContextInfo.quotedMessage` with the quote, so a receiver that does not
hold the original still shows what was quoted. Empty sends none. The core
looks nothing up. Bytes with no `quote.quoted` are InvalidArgument, and so
are bytes that are not a `wa.Message`.

messages.name: ServerAckEvent
messages.comment:
The server's own verdict on one outgoing stanza, relayed verbatim.

Issue #4: SendResult means "the relay handed the message to the library",
which is NOT the same as "the server took it" — a send whose device fan-out
comes out empty answers with a real key and puts nothing on the wire. The
core cannot see inside that fan-out, so it relays the only authority that
can settle it: the `<ack>` itself.

Correlate `id` with `SendResult.key.id`. No ServerAck for a message id means
the server never took it. How long to wait before calling that a failure is
edge policy — a timeout in the core would be exactly the "if X did not
happen in N seconds" rule the core does not own.

`error` is the nack code (e.g. "479") when the server REJECTED the stanza;
empty on a plain ack.

fields.name: class
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Stanza class: "message", "receipt", "notification", "call", ... Empty when
the server omits it.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
Server timestamp (ms). For a message ack this is the authoritative send
time. 0 when the server omitted it.

messages.name: SetAboutRequest
messages.comment: The account's OWN about text, relayed as given: "" is sent as is (#197).

messages.name: SetGroupPhotoRequest
messages.comment: Set or remove a group's photo. An empty `image` means "remove the photo".

messages.name: StanzaNode
messages.comment:
A server stanza as the library received it, relayed whole (#138): the core
does not parse it, so data the library leaves alone (an account lock's
one-time `appeal_token`, `violation_reason`, `vt`) still reaches the edge.
Reading it is edge policy.

`attrs` holds every attribute as text; a jid-valued attribute carries its
wire form ("5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net"). The binary protocol does not
forbid a repeated key; if one ever arrives, the last value wins.

`content` keeps the library's three shapes apart: `bytes` for binary
content, `text` for content the codec read as a string, `children` for
child elements in order (an empty list when the element had an empty child
list). Unset when the element had no content at all.

Depth: each level costs two nested messages (StanzaNode, StanzaNodeList).
A prost client decodes at most 100 nested messages, so a stanza deeper than
about 47 levels cannot be decoded there. The core relays what the library
decoded (up to 128 levels) without cutting it; real logout and ban stanzas
are two or three levels deep.

messages.name: StanzaNodeList
messages.comment:
The child elements of a StanzaNode, in the order the server sent them. A
message of its own because a oneof cannot hold a repeated field.

messages.name: StarChange
messages.comment:
A message was starred or unstarred. `AppStateUpdate.chat` is the chat that
holds it.

fields.name: participant
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The sender, for someone else's message in a group; unset for your own
message or in a direct chat.

messages.name: StarMessageRequest
messages.comment:
target.chat = the chat; target.participant = sender inside a group (unset
in a DM); target.id = message id; target.from_me = whether we sent it.

fields.name: starred
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true=star, false=unstar

messages.name: StatusAudience
messages.comment:
One status audience mode. The library keeps this enum open, so a number it
does not know crosses as UNKNOWN with the number in `mode_code` (0 otherwise).

messages.name: StatusAudienceResponse
messages.comment:
The account's status audience as the library last synced it from the phone
(#89): the same `StatusPrivacySetting` an `AccountSettingUpdate` carries, read
back on demand, because the event only comes live or from the full sync at
pairing and an edge that missed it has no other way to recover it.

`audience` unset means no audience has been synced yet. That is NOT "all
contacts", and neither is an UNKNOWN mode. The audience is informative: a
status still goes to exactly the `recipients` the edge posts it to.

messages.name: StatusCustomList
messages.comment: A custom status audience list.

fields.name: users
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment: an empty entry is skipped

messages.name: StatusPrivacySetting
messages.comment:
The account's status audience (`status_privacy`). Measured live 2026-10-08:
"my contacts except..." sends `mode` DENY_LIST with the excluded users and
`modes` [DENY_LIST]; back to "my contacts" sends CONTACTS and no users. An
UNKNOWN mode is not "all contacts".

fields.name: mode
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: unset when the mutation had none

fields.name: users
fields.label: repeated
fields.comment:
The allow or deny list, as the mutation lists it; an empty entry is
skipped, as in FavoritesChanged.

messages.name: StickerAudio
messages.comment:
The clip of a sound sticker, relayed as the sticker's AudioMessage. Each
field relays verbatim; proto3 defaults are the absent field.

fields.name: mime_type
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: e.g. "audio/ogg; codecs=opus"

messages.name: StickerPackInfo
messages.comment:
A received sticker pack, as its StickerPackMessage states it. The pack is ONE
encrypted file, a ZIP holding each sticker under its `file_name` plus the tray
icon; unzipping it is the edge's business, the core relays the bytes.

fields.name: pack_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the maker app's id, verbatim

fields.name: tray_icon_file_name
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the tray icon's entry in the ZIP

fields.name: pack_size
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
`stickerPackSize` verbatim. NOT the archive's length, which is
`media.file_length`: the two differ (501503 vs 501859 on the pack #58 was
measured on), and upstream does not document what this one counts.

fields.name: thumbnail
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The pack's thumbnail, a second file encrypted under the pack's media key,
under MEDIA_TYPE_STICKER_PACK_THUMBNAIL: DownloadMedia takes it as is.
Unset when the message names no thumbnail path. Its `file_length` is 0
because the message does not declare one; the download is still verified
by both hashes and the MAC.

messages.name: StickerUpdate
messages.comment:
A sticker mutation on a linked device (#148): favorited, unfavorited, or
removed from the recent list.

Not an AppStateUpdate: stickers belong to the account, not to a chat, and
the mutation carries no time of its own beside `timestamp`.

fields.name: filehash
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: WA Web's sticker key: the base64 SHA-256 of the decrypted file, verbatim.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: mutation time (ms)

fields.name: from_full_sync
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: true when replayed by a full app-state sync

messages.name: StreamErrorInfo
messages.comment:
A `<stream:error>` the library does not act on as a logout or a takeover:
a 429 (rate limited; the library backs off and reconnects) or a code it does
not know. The connection is kept.

fields.name: code
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: verbatim; empty when the stanza carried none (e.g. `<ack/>`)

fields.name: stanza
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the whole `<stream:error>`

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
How long the server keeps pushing, in seconds. Measured live: 90. The
library answers 300 when the server omits the attribute; that fallback is
its, not the server's.

fields.name: all_accounts
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
"all" is DYNAMIC: it includes accounts created after subscribing, so the
stream stays open until the client hangs up or the daemon shuts down.
On shutdown (SIGTERM) every subscription, "all" or per-account, ends
with a clean end of stream (status OK) rather than a torn connection:
the daemon is going away, reconnect when the socket is back. Under an
extreme burst of creates the
core may emit a `subscription_gap` RawEvent meaning some newly created
accounts are missing from the stream: re-subscribe or reconcile via
ListAccounts.

fields.name: replay_from_ring
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
0 = live only; N = replay up to N buffered events for quick reconnect.
No duplicates within one stream: live events already delivered by the
replay are skipped (filtered by monotonic_seq). Accounts created AFTER an
all-accounts subscribe always replay their full ring regardless of N —
"live only" cannot apply to events emitted before their forwarder
attached, so e.g. a just-created account's pairing QR is never lost.

messages.name: SyncMessageRange
messages.comment:
Which messages a chat mutation covers (`wa.SyncActionValue.SyncActionMessageRange`).
The server counts these in seconds (measured live 2026-10-07: the last
message's own time); the core converts them to ms.

fields.name: last_message_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

fields.name: last_system_message_timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment:
Never seen set; read with the same unit as its sibling.
ms

fields.name: timestamp
fields.label: optional
fields.comment: ms

messages.name: TemplateReply
messages.comment: Answers a `templateMessage`.

fields.name: selected_id
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: templateButtonReplyMessage.selectedId

fields.name: selected_index
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The button's position, and 0 is the FIRST one, not "unset": the captured
reply carries an explicit 0. Relayed as-is, never folded away by the rule
that maps proto3 zero defaults to an absent waproto field.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: The server's numeric code, only when `reason` is UNKNOWN. 0 otherwise.

fields.name: expire_seconds
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
How long the ban lasts, in seconds, as the server's `expire` says: a
duration, not a deadline.

fields.name: message
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the server's `message` attribute; empty when absent

fields.name: url
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: the support/appeal link; empty when absent

fields.name: stanza
fields.label: singular
fields.comment:
The whole `<failure>` stanza the ban came in (#138), for anything the
fields above do not carry. Unset when the library had none.

messages.name: UnarchiveChatsSetting
messages.comment:
The "keep chats archived" setting (#215). The flag is the inverse of the
phone's switch: `unarchive_chats` is true when "keep chats archived" is OFF,
so a new message moves its chat out of the archive. The library emits the
update only when the wire carried the flag, so it is never a default.

messages.name: UserStatusMuteChange
messages.comment:
A contact's status updates were hidden from, or shown again in, the status
list. `AppStateUpdate.chat` is the contact. Measured: hiding sends
`muted` true; showing again sent nothing in two tries.

fields.name: pn
fields.label: singular
fields.comment: unset when absent

enums.name: BanReason
enums.comment: The temporary-ban codes the library names (code in comment).

enums.name: BlobFormat
enums.comment:
The format the store's structured blobs are in (the `blob_format` marker,
#31). 0.2.x is the last release line that converts a bincode store; 0.3.0
refuses one (#84), so check this reads PROTOBUF before upgrading past 0.2.

values.name: BLOB_FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED
values.comment: the store did not answer, or the marker is unknown

enums.name: BusinessDayOfWeek
enums.comment:
The library names seven days and keeps any other token, so UNKNOWN carries
that token in `day_of_week_raw`.

enums.name: BusinessHourMode
enums.comment: Same rule: UNKNOWN carries the server's token in `mode_raw`.

enums.name: BusinessUpdateType
enums.comment:
`wacore::types::events::BusinessUpdateType`. UNKNOWN is the library's own
`Unknown`: it does not keep the wire string, so there is no code.

values.name: CALL_LINK_MEDIA_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

enums.name: CallLogResult
enums.comment: `wa.CallLogRecord.CallResult`.

values.name: CALL_LOG_RESULT_UNKNOWN
values.comment: a variant this build does not name

enums.name: CallLogSilenceReason
enums.comment: `wa.CallLogRecord.SilenceReason`.

values.name: CALL_LOG_SILENCE_REASON_UNKNOWN
values.comment: a variant this build does not name

enums.name: CallLogType
enums.comment: `wa.CallLogRecord.CallType`.

values.name: CALL_LOG_TYPE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: a variant this build does not name

enums.name: ChatState
enums.comment:
The library models "recording" as composing with audio media; the contract
keeps the three states the edge draws. No raw: the library never hands the
activity over as a number.

values.name: CHAT_STATE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: an activity this build does not name

enums.name: DeviceListChangeType
enums.comment: `wacore::types::events::DeviceListUpdateType`, closed in the library.

enums.name: EditAttribute
enums.comment:
A message's `edit` attribute (#128), the library's `EditAttribute`. The
numbers are not the server's: the server's token is in each comment.

values.name: GROUP_ADDRESSING_MODE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

values.name: GROUP_APPEAL_STATUS_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

enums.name: GroupHistorySentState
enums.comment: Whether a new member got the group's history. A closed library set.

values.name: GROUP_HISTORY_SENT_STATE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

values.name: GROUP_MEMBER_ADD_MODE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

values.name: GROUP_MEMBER_LINK_MODE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

values.name: GROUP_MEMBER_SHARE_HISTORY_MODE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

values.name: GROUP_PARTICIPANT_TYPE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

enums.name: JoinOutcome
enums.comment:
What the library reported for an accepted invite (`JoinGroupResult`): a closed
set of two, so no raw fallback.

values.name: JOIN_OUTCOME_PENDING_APPROVAL
values.comment: The group requires admin approval: the account is not a member yet.

enums.name: LabelListType
enums.comment: `wa.SyncActionValue.LabelEditAction.ListType`.

values.name: LABEL_LIST_TYPE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: a list type this build does not name

enums.name: LogoutReason
enums.comment: The server's `<failure>` reason codes the library names (code in comment).

values.name: LOGOUT_REASON_UNKNOWN_LOGOUT
values.comment: 406, a code the server sends, not UNKNOWN

enums.name: MediaType
enums.comment:
The kind of a media payload (#127). A closed set: the core builds every
descriptor from its own kinds, so UNKNOWN is never emitted and there is no
raw field. On a request, UNSPECIFIED, UNKNOWN and any value the operation
does not take are InvalidArgument.

values.name: MEDIA_TYPE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: never emitted; refused on a request

enums.name: MembershipRequestMethod
enums.comment:
How a join request was made. A closed library set (it reads an unknown
token as INVITE_LINK), so UNKNOWN is never emitted.

values.name: MEMBERSHIP_REQUEST_METHOD_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

enums.name: MissedCallReason
enums.comment:
`wacore::types::call::MissedReason`, non_exhaustive in the library: a reason
it adds later crosses as UNKNOWN.

values.name: MISSED_CALL_REASON_OFFLINE
values.comment: an offer replayed from the offline queue

values.name: MISSED_CALL_REASON_REMOTE
values.comment:
A terminate for a call never answered. Needs the library's `voip-control`
feature, which this build does not enable.

enums.name: NewsletterMessageType
enums.comment:
The `type` the server labelled a history row with (#128). Measured live:
text, media, poll. The library names five more that its own docs say the
wire never produces; a row carrying one of those, or any other token, is
UNKNOWN with the token in `type_raw`.

enums.name: NewsletterPollType
enums.comment: `<meta polltype>` (#128), the library's closed `PollType`.

enums.name: NewsletterRole
enums.comment:
This account's role in the channel (#128). No raw: the library drops a role
it does not model, and UNKNOWN is only a variant it adds later.

enums.name: NewsletterState
enums.comment:
The channel's state (#128). A deleted channel is UNKNOWN with `DELETED` in
`state_raw`.

enums.name: NewsletterVerification
enums.comment:
The channel's verification badge (#128). Closed in practice; the library
keeps an unmodelled value as the server spelled it, which relays in
`verification_raw`.

enums.name: PairCodeRejection
enums.comment: `wacore::pair_code::PairCodeRejection`, open in the library (code in comment).

values.name: PAIR_CODE_REJECTION_BAD_REQUEST
values.comment:
400. The server also uses it to throttle a phone number, so it is not
reliably permanent.

enums.name: PresenceState
enums.comment:
What SendPresence raises: AVAILABLE and UNAVAILABLE are the account's own
presence, not scoped to `chat`; the other three are a chat state in `chat`.
UNSPECIFIED and UNKNOWN are InvalidArgument: a request has no raw field.

enums.name: ReceiptType
enums.comment:
Every receipt type the library names. One it does not name arrives as
UNKNOWN with the attribute in `type_raw`.

values.name: SCREEN_SHARE_STATE_UNKNOWN
values.comment: not emitted today: the set is closed

enums.name: StatusAudienceMode
enums.comment: `wa.SyncActionValue.StatusPrivacyAction.StatusDistributionMode`.

enums.name: StickerPackOrigin
enums.comment:
One sticker inside a received pack, as the pack message lists it. `file_name`
is its entry in the ZIP, so an edge can match metadata to bytes after
unzipping.
The decoder drops a number it does not know, so such a pack reads UNSPECIFIED
and the number survives only in `raw_message`. UNKNOWN is a variant this
build does not name yet. That is why there is no `origin_raw`.

values.name: STICKER_PACK_ORIGIN_UNKNOWN
values.comment: a variant this build does not name

enums.name: UnavailableReason
enums.comment:
Why the message could not be decrypted, as the library classifies the
stanza. The library's set is closed and has its own "unknown" (a stanza with
no recognised flag), which is UNKNOWN here; there is no raw to relay.
